limitations.message: Advective screening plugin is deterministic and screening-oriented.
Advective screening plugin adds first-order advective clearance but does not model spatial gradients or explicit intermedia transfer coefficients.
Advective_screening_mass_balance uses deterministic finite-duration first-order screening math with degradation plus advective clearance within one compartment per medium.
Some scenario parameters are preserved for provenance and assessor review but are not consumed by the current runtime.
One or more manifest entries rely on heuristic source classification.
Uncertainty summary ranks deterministic reviewer-facing drivers only and does not provide Monte Carlo outputs, confidence intervals, or probabilistic bounds.
Some runtime outputs depend on curated defaults rather than scenario-specific measurements.
Scientific review packet summarizes screening-oriented methods support only and is not a statement of regulator acceptance or submission approval.

summary_lines: Build a composed scientific dossier that couples the governed model-family challenge review path with model-family-specific scientific review packets.
Challenge review status model_family_challenge_review_attention_needed governs scenario scenario-306863db9176.
Primary family reference_mass_balance scientific review outcome: qualified_screening_use.
Challenge family advective_screening_mass_balance scientific review outcome: qualified_screening_use.
recommended_actions: Use reference_mass_balance as the baseline run and compare it against advective_screening_mass_balance using comparison profile reference_vs_advective_screening_v1.
Treat the advective family as experimental and non-default even when it is recommended as a challenge path.
Use the governed comparison profile to compare reference and advective outputs before carrying the candidate family into assessor-facing review.
Do not skip the reference baseline when a challenge family is recommended.
Keep the selection recommendation in assessor-facing attention status until the governed challenge-path, applicability, or packet-check concerns are resolved.
Treat the candidate family as experimental and keep the default reference family as the screening baseline unless the transport question clearly requires the candidate assumptions.
Review the dominant surface deltas, residence-time assumptions, and equation traces before choosing which family better matches the decision context.
Use this comparison profile when the reference family is the screening baseline and the advective family is being challenged on the same scenario.
Interpret the candidate family as experimental and non-default even when the comparison shows material differences.
Escalate to richer transport methods when the decision context is dominated by spatial hydrodynamics or intermedia transfer.
Keep the comparison in assessor-facing attention status until the governed divergence, experimental-family, or packet-check concerns are resolved.
Keep the composed model-family challenge review in assessor-facing attention status until the governed selection-review or comparison-review concerns are resolved.
Carry the qualification notes and limitation lines forward in assessor-facing summaries.
Document where governed defaults drove the result and consider scenario-specific overrides for sensitive decisions.
Document when governed screening capacities dominate the concentration scaling and whether scenario-specific capacities are available.
Consider a richer model family if intermedia dynamics are central to the decision context.
Do not treat preserved-only parameters as if they were actively modeled by the runtime.
Consider a richer model family if spatial hydrodynamics or intermedia exchange dominate the decision context.
